title: Chicken Rice Bowls
headnote: Soy-garlic chicken over rice with roasted sweet potatoes and a cool, lemony yogurt sauce. Most of it can be made on prep day.
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Toss the sweet potatoes with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes.
Season the chicken with the soy sauce and garlic. Sear in the remaining oil with the onion until cooked through, about 12 minutes.
Stir the yogurt and lemon juice together into a sauce.
Divide the rice, chicken and sweet potatoes among bowls and drizzle with the sauce.

title: Turkey Patties with Yogurt Sauce
headnote: Herby turkey patties with a cool cucumber-dill sauce. The sauce and the chopping can be done ahead.
steps: Mix the turkey, onion, garlic, egg, panko and salt and form into 8 patties.
Stir the yogurt, cucumber, lemon juice and dill together into a sauce.
Cook the patties in the oiled skillet over medium-high heat, 5 minutes per side, until cooked through.
Serve warm with plenty of sauce.

title: Simple Tomato Pasta
headnote: A weeknight spaghetti with soft, garlicky tomatoes and plenty of basil. Nothing fancy, always welcome.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente. Toss with the tomatoes, basil and Parmesan.

title: Miso-Glazed Cod
headnote: Broiled cod with a sweet-salty miso glaze, served with rice and bok choy. Dinner in about twenty-five minutes.
steps: Whisk the miso, honey and soy sauce into a glaze.
Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Heat the broiler. Brush the cod with the glaze and broil 8 to 10 minutes, until flaky.
Sauté the bok choy in the oil for 3 minutes.
Serve the cod with the rice and bok choy and top with the scallions.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken & Sweet Potatoes
headnote: Garlic-lemon chicken thighs roasted on one pan with sweet potatoes, red onion and broccoli. Minimal dishes.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the chicken, sweet potatoes, onion and broccoli with the oil, garlic and salt on a large sheet pan.
Tuck in the lemon slices and roast for 35 minutes, until the chicken is crisp and the vegetables are tender.

title: Black Bean Patties
headnote: Crispy cumin-spiced black bean patties on buns with a cilantro yogurt sauce.
ingredients: 2 (15-oz) cans black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Mash the black beans in a large bowl. Mix in the onion, garlic, egg, panko, cumin and half the cilantro.
Form into 4 patties and chill for 10 minutes.
Pan-fry the patties in the oil, 4 minutes per side.
Stir the yogurt and the remaining cilantro together into a sauce.
Serve the patties on buns with the sauce.

title: Salmon Bowls
headnote: Seared salmon over rice with cucumber, avocado and a soy-sesame dressing. The dressing keeps for days.
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Whisk the soy sauce and rice vinegar into a dressing.
Sear the salmon skin-side down in the oil for 5 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Build bowls with the rice, salmon, cucumber and avocado. Drizzle with the dressing and top with the scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
headnote: The best use for leftover rice. Cook the rice a day ahead and dinner takes ten minutes.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, diced
steps: Cook the rice the day before and chill it, or use leftover rice.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the neutral oil in a large skillet over high heat. Cook the chicken until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic, ginger and scallions and stir for 30 seconds. Add the peas and carrots and cook 2 minutes.
Push everything aside and scramble the eggs in the pan. Add the rice, chicken, soy sauce and sesame oil and stir-fry for 3 minutes.

title: Weeknight Chicken Curry
headnote: A mild, creamy curry built from pantry staples. Serve over rice with plenty of cilantro.
ingredients: 1½ lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 6 minutes, then stir in the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the chicken, tomatoes, coconut milk and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Serve over the rice, topped with the cilantro.

title: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Tacos
headnote: Roasted sweet potatoes and warm black beans in corn tortillas, finished with lime and cilantro.
ingredients: 1 (15-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, chili powder, cumin and salt. Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes, until tender and browned.
Warm the beans in a small saucepan over low heat.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet.
Fill the tortillas with the sweet potatoes and beans and top with the red onion, cilantro, sliced avocado and a squeeze of lime.

title: Sheet-Pan Sausage & Vegetables
headnote: Smoked sausage, potatoes and broccoli roasted together until browned at the edges. Easy cleanup.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes, broccoli, bell pepper, onion and sausage with the oil, paprika and salt on two sheet pans.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until the potatoes are golden and tender.

title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
headnote: Tender sliced steak and crisp broccoli in a glossy ginger-garlic sauce. Whisk the sauce ahead and dinner is fast.
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Whisk the soy sauce, brown sugar, cornstarch and water into a sauce.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the steak in two batches, 2 minutes per batch, and transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, the garlic, the ginger and the broccoli with 2 tablespoons of water. Cover and steam for 3 minutes.
Return the steak to the pan, pour in the sauce and cook until glossy, about 1 minute. Serve over the rice.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup
headnote: Pantry-friendly tomato soup that blends smooth in minutes. Good with a grilled cheese.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar and salt. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. Stir in the cream and season to taste.
Serve topped with torn basil.
